CausalChain: Fasting -> metabolic stress -> activation of AMPK -> downregulation of glycolytic enzymes (HK2, PFKFB3, PKM2) -> shift from aerobic glycolysis to OXPHOS -> reduced lactate production and extracellular acidification -> alleviation of tumor-induced immunosuppression -> enhanced efficacy of PD-1/PD-L1 blockade
Hypothesis: Fasting-induced AMPK activation in HCC reprograms tumor metabolism away from aerobic glycolysis, thereby reducing lactate-mediated immunosuppression and sensitizing tumors to PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint therapy.
Abstract: In hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the predominance of aerobic glycolysis not only fuels rapid tumor growth but also contributes to an immunosuppressive microenvironment through lactate-mediated acidification. We propose that fasting, by inducing metabolic stress and subsequent AMPK activation, may reprogram HCC metabolism from a glycolytic to an oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) phenotype. This metabolic shift would reduce lactate production and extracellular acidification, subsequently alleviating local immunosuppression. In turn, the improved immune milieu could enhance the efficacy of PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint blockade in treating HCC. This hypothesis provides a rationale for combining fasting or metabolic stress inducers with immune checkpoint inhibitors to overcome resistance and improve therapeutic outcomes in HCC.
